## Left and Right Shift

Let k be the desired number of shifts. Create a masking vector with 1s in the $k$ elements from the end shifted away from (on the right side for a left shift, and vice versa). Cycle your target vector by $k$, then multiply your target vector with the masking vector. 
$c = (0_0, /dots 0_{n-k-1}, 1_{},1_{n})$

What happens with an overshift?
This can depend on implementation. One solution may be to throw an error, while another would be to zero out the target vector for any $k\geq n$.

## XOR
Boolean XOR can be expressed as $a+b-2ab$ or $(a-b)^2$, all of which are basic moves. No modular reduction is needed in computation, but we must assume we are receiving valid input. For maximum efficiency of an intravector XOR, use a similar technique as with intravector addition.
